RoboChrono is a real-robot benchmark for streaming task understanding: 39 scenarios, 34,713 instances and ~25 hours of synchronized head- and wrist-camera video from two dual-arm platforms, with seven causal QA tasks (current/next action, frame and view matching, frame ordering, action time localization) evaluated on 18 VLMs.

**Highlights**

- Best model (GPT-6-Astra) reaches 80.5% average but only 68.3% on Frame Ordering; best open model 62.8%.
- Input ablations show next-action prediction leans on task priors rather than vision.

**My contributions**

- Led VR-teleoperation data collection on GIM's dual-arm whole-workspace platform.
- Designed the human-annotation and QA-template protocol that converts action/state intervals into the seven benchmark tasks.
- Built the VLM evaluation harness and ran the zero-shot evaluation sweep.
- Led results analysis and co-wrote the paper.
- Contributed to scenario design, camera synchronization, input ablations, and the Hugging Face dataset release (gimai/RC-GIM).
